text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- German-Czech declaration approved with large majority in German lower house.
- Officials within ruling Christian Democrats (CDU) meet to discuss crisis in the party.
- Origin of cow which prompted BSE scare becoming more and - Confederation of German Industry (BDI) says its members could be the big losers in government's tax reform plans.
- Transport Minister Matthias Wissmann insists government still behind Transrapid high-speed rail project.
HANDELSBLATT
- Government awards public telephone operating licences to Mannesmann Arcor AG and Teleglobe GmbH.
- Robert Bosch increased turnover by 15 percent last year to 5.4 billion marks.
- More and more experts believe European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) will start on time.
- German chambers of commerce abroad more efficient than embassies, economics ministry says.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Labour Minister Norbert Bluem says he cannot rely on Chancellor Helmut Kohl for help to push through his pension reform plans.
- Deutsche Telekom board member Gerd Tenzer says company will have most modern network in the world by the end of the year.
- Production in east German mechanical engineering sector increases but job cuts continue.
DIE WELT
- CDU officials discuss possible successors to Labour Minister Bluem.
- Government and opposition do not plan talks on tax reform.
- IG Metall trade union threatens huge protests if employers try to change wage-negotiating system.
- Opposition and government at loggerheads over funding for alternative energy projects.
-- Bonn Newsroom +49 228 26097160
